wp-1.1.summary: Phase 1 (Every kind of task on both executors). The pair table, and briefs chosen by executor. See WP3.1, WP3.4, WP3.5; §D3.
acceptance: A test fails when a pair of executor and kind is missing from the table; every cell's brief runs through a fake executor of its kind to a recorded result; no `process` brief holds "commit", "push" or "runner report"; the existing delivery, batch and worker-mode tests pass with their assertions unchanged.

wp-1.2.summary: Phase 1 (Every kind of task on both executors). Findings by the command line and by the result file. See WP3.2, WP4.2; §D4.
acceptance: Tests with fake executors: a chat's findings by the command line and a child's findings by the result file open the same falsifier request and the same gate; Go ahead resumes the same child session and its done result lands; a findings file over the size limit is refused; a done result before Go ahead is still refused; a definition with no `resume` codes the task without the step and shows why.

wp-1.3.summary: Phase 1 (Every kind of task on both executors). A batch on `process` runs as single tasks. See WP3.3; §D3.
acceptance: Tests: a three-task group on `process` starts three sessions and lands three commits, and the page and `avoozl show` give the reason; the same group on `kirocrew` still runs in one chat with one commit per task.

wp-1.4.summary: Phase 1 (Every kind of task on both executors). A report command that needs no `PATH`, and no MCP tool in a worker's brief. See WP4.1, WP4.3, WP4.5; §D5.
acceptance: A test runs the report command taken from a built brief in a shell with an empty `PATH`, against the source checkout and against the built app package, and both record the report; a search of every `kirocrew` worker brief in the pair table finds no `plans_`; `plans_report` from a verifier and from an MCP client Avoozl did not start still works.

wp-p1.summary: Phase 1 (Every kind of task on both executors). Proof: every pair of executor and task kind reaches a result. See WP3, WP4; §D3, §D4, §D5.
acceptance: Expected: (1) every task lands on both executors, the batch as one chat on `kirocrew` and as three children on `process`; (2) each investigated task codes only after Go ahead, in the same session it investigated in; (3) no brief names an MCP tool or a bare `avoozl`, and no `process` brief asks for a commit; MCP sharing for `avoozl:avoozl` is off for the whole `kirocrew` run.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

wp-2.1.summary: Phase 2 (The manual path without Crew Mode). A person claims a task with the tick on. See WP2.1, WP2.2, WP2.3, WP2.4, WP2.5, WP2.7; §D6.
acceptance: Tests with the tick on: a claimed task stays unstarted across three ticks; `runner report` from its worktree with no token finishes it and Avoozl runs the checks; a claim is refused for a task that is not ready, has a running session or is held by Stop the line, each with its reason; a claim over MCP and from a child of the supervisor is refused; release refuses a dirty worktree without `--discard`.

wp-2.2.summary: Phase 2 (The manual path without Crew Mode). Remove Crew Mode dispatch, and hold the workspaces that used it. See WP1.1, WP1.2, WP1.3, WP1.4, WP2.6, WP7.4, WP7.5; §D7.
acceptance: Tests: a `crew-mode` workspace starts nothing across three ticks and shows one Needs you item; the operation is refused from MCP and from an agent session, and from a person it removes the key and the next tick starts work; `"runner": "tick"` loads and is ignored; the source test of WP1.4 passes and fails on a planted second dispatcher; the pull request lists what each moved or deleted test covered and where it is covered now; the schema parity test passes.

wp-p2.summary: Phase 2 (The manual path without Crew Mode). Proof: a person finishes a task by hand while the tick runs the rest. See WP1, WP2; §D6, §D7.
acceptance: Expected: (1) the claim prints the worktree and the report command; (2) the tick starts the other task only; (3) Avoozl runs the checks on the commit and lands it; (4) the released task is ready again and the next tick starts it.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

wp-3.1.summary: Phase 3 (One remote route). A worker machine pulls and claims on its own tick. See WP5.2; §D8.
acceptance: Tests with a fake GitHub and a fake driver: a worker with two free lanes and three offers claims two and starts two with no command run by hand; a request with no acknowledgment starts nothing; a tick with no GitHub records one line and starts nothing; the hand-run commands give the same result as one tick.

wp-3.2.summary: Phase 3 (One remote route). The driver checks a pulled result on its tick. See WP5.3; §D8.
acceptance: Tests: a pushed result lands with no command run by hand; a result that touches a protected path, and one whose checks fail on the driver, each become a failed attempt on the driver with the reason; a result for a claim the driver did not acknowledge is ignored; `worker-results.mjs` has an importer that is not a test.

wp-3.3.summary: Phase 3 (One remote route). Remove runner mode over SSH. See WP5.1, WP5.4, WP5.5; §D8.
acceptance: Tests: a file with `runner.role: "runner"` or `"driver"` is refused naming the key and worker pull; an envelope is taken only from an acknowledged claim; a search of `src/` finds no `ssh` argv outside the plugin and mirror code; the pull request lists what the deleted tests covered and where it is covered now.

wp-p3.summary: Phase 3 (One remote route). Proof: two workspaces, one driver and one worker, with only ticks. See WP5; §D8.
acceptance: Expected: (1) and (2) both tasks land on the driver's base branch and no `worker` command was run by hand; (3) the driver refuses it as a failed attempt and nothing lands.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

wp-4.1.summary: Phase 4 (Sessions run on this machine). Remove remote crews and the hand-back. See WP6.1, WP6.2, WP6.6; §D9.
acceptance: Remove remote crews and the hand-back
The remote steps, `handback.mjs`, `kirocrewRemoteSession` and the `crew` argument of the executor are gone. The crew snapshot stays.

wp-4.2.summary: Phase 4 (Sessions run on this machine). Delivery shows what holds a task. See WP6.3; §D9.
acceptance: Delivery shows what holds a task
Delivery shows the lane limit and each provider check that holds a task.

wp-5.1.summary: Phase 5 (Names). Removed commands answer with their replacement. See WP7.1, WP7.2, WP7.3; §D7, §D8, §D9.
acceptance: A test calls each removed command and operation and gets one line naming its replacement and no change to the workspace; the help test passes; the `plans_*` tool names, the environment aliases and the `aicommander` command pass their existing tests.

wp-5.2.summary: Phase 5 (Names). One meaning for each word, and the product spec says the same. See WP8, WP9; §D1.
acceptance: The word test passes and fails on a planted "Crew Mode"; `node scripts/spec-lint.mjs` reports 0 errors; each retired requirement keeps its text under a dated line naming this spec.

wp-p4.summary: Phase 5 (Names). Proof: one dispatcher, two executors, one remote route. See WP1 to WP9; §D1.
acceptance: Expected: (1) both pass; (2) the list is the tick's planner and the manual claim; (3) nothing is found, which holds only once task 45.4 of the avoozl spec has landed; (4) the receipt records the two counts and the modules that went.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.
